notes: `בָנִים לְבָנֶיךָ` → *thy children's children*: the `לְ` has no English word of its own and its relation is written inside the genitive *children's*, so rule 30's one-rendering condition is met and the two morphemes share a unit under rule 49's closing sentence, headed on `בָנֶי`, which carries the lexeme. Checked as a multi-source unit: the pair is indivisible, since no target token answers to the preposition apart from the possessive marker on the noun's own word.

The competing reading marks the `לְ` `unrepresented` under rule 40, on the analogy of a dative recast as a bare possessive determiner. It was set aside because rule 40's own boundary sentence reserves that outcome for a case where the English pronoun is the word a bare suffix takes in any event, whereas here the genitive marker is written on a word that would otherwise stand bare.

`שָׁלוֹם עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵל`: the clause writes no subject but the one nominal and the ASV writes no separate English subject, so `שָׁלוֹם` is the subject and the prepositional phrase the predicate; the copula stays on the `עַל` and the unit heads on *upon*, under rule 49's closing paragraph.
The ASV margin offers *Or, And peace upon Israel* for the last colon. It was read and set aside under rule 38: the printed text governs, and it writes the copula.
